what: STMicroelectronics makes chips for cars, industrial equipment and consumer devices: microcontrollers, power semiconductors including silicon carbide, sensors and analogue chips. It is European, with plants in France and Italy.
customers: Carmakers and their suppliers, industrial equipment manufacturers, and consumer electronics companies including smartphone makers.
money: Analog, Power and Discrete, MEMS and Sensors
power chips, silicon carbide and sensors
microcontrollers for cars and industry, plus radio frequency chips
moat: Designed-in positions in car platforms and industrial equipment that last for the product's life, plus one of the few Western silicon carbide manufacturing bases.
risks: Revenue fell about 11% last year and about 10% a year over three years
Operating margin collapsed to about 1% as factories ran below capacity
European car production has been falling
Chinese silicon carbide competitors are driving prices down
opportunities: Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Cash of about $5 billion exceeds its debt, so it can ride out the downturn
Industrial and automotive chip inventories have largely been worked off
watch: Quarterly revenue against the bottom of the cycle, and factory utilisation.
